source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-19:45 (tools/video_draft.py transcript CLKfTRiFbJA --start 0 --end 1170), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; nothing past 19:45 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates; 'related' lists looser topic matches. Solo draft: every idea is the host's (speaker field kept for the schema).

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Heartwood Crafter keeps beating him when opponents play it: a turn-one Crafter plus the soul-tether token lets them cast giant creatures fast with a 1/1 that pays for activated abilities.
ideas.quote: They go this turn one, turn two, they get the soul tether going and then they just start like casting giant creatures pretty fast.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Heartwood Crafter in ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Kiora of Fire and Ashes is an easy pick in a ramp deck: Crafter ramps to Kiora and leaves the extra mana for her activated ability.
ideas.quote: Kiora is pretty easy pick. I do also like Rescue Girl.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Kiora of Fire and Ashes with Heartwood Crafter or other ramp.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Thalia, the Survivor is obnoxious: it adds cost to your curve and the opponent does not always see the impact.
ideas.quote: It just adds a lot of costs to your curve and it's deceptive because you don't always see the impact it has on your opponent.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Thalia, the Survivor and win rate against it.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Take the top-end card and save the two-drops for later: Edgar, Moonlit Sovereign over Vigorbloom Vanguard, because Edgar can hold mana and grow.
ideas.quote: I'm going to try taking the Edgar. Get a like nice top end card. Save the two drops for later.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Edgar, Moonlit Sovereign against Vigorbloom Vanguard.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Pick the colour you want to bias towards: Wrath of the Bloodmane over Rescue Girl because he wants to end up in red, even though Rescue Girl works with Kiora.
ideas.quote: I would love to just bias towards red if I can. And so, I'm going to do that by taking the Wrath of the Blood Mane.
ideas.test_idea: Whether biasing towards the open colour beats the stronger off-colour card at pick 4.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Read missing cards in a pack: three cards are gone and two must have been a pair, so the black Rescue Girl or Massacre Girl went; no good black cards seen.
ideas.quote: There's three cards missing in this pack and two of them must have been part of a pair.
ideas.test_idea: Whether the missing pair partner predicts what the upstream drafter took.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: No Admittance is just fantastic and a sign red is open: a few good red cards arrive in a row.
ideas.quote: No Admittance is just fantastic. Easy pick up. I think red is looking to be open here.
ideas.test_idea: Whether a P1p5 No Admittance predicts red decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: He has not had a two-drop; a 'one, two, three, four, five, six' curve of rares is rare; take the two-drop (Sureshot Sower) over an ambitious splash, because splashing too ambitiously is his usual mistake.
ideas.quote: I feel like I've been like a bit too ambitious with trying to splash.
ideas.test_idea: Splash play rate by pick position of the first splash card.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Splashing too much is a drafting habit: when a very good two-colour deck shows itself, speculative greedy picks into other colours lead to over-splashing (a Stark / LSV story).
ideas.quote: it's like the way your draft and like your approach is leaning towards that a little bit much.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of two-colour decks against decks with a splash, controlling for skill.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: When nothing in the pack matters to a settled red-green deck, take a speculative card: he does not love Keeper of the Quiet Hour or Blazing Crescendo and has ten good cards already.
ideas.quote: I do think I'm kind of set on red green and I don't really mind just being like okay I have 10 good cards. I'm just going to take this as a speculative.
ideas.test_idea: Not testable.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Face Yourself needs a planeswalker he will not control often, so it would not stick around; Jiang Yanggu, Alone is better because his creatures hold back on defense and it gets rid of extra lands.
ideas.quote: I'm not going to control a planeswalker a ton. I don't have a ton of Empower Jace.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Face Yourself by number of Empower Jace cards.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Violent Echoes is a really good removal spell that lets him empower Jace and may draw a card if it kills a three-toughness creature.
ideas.quote: Really good removal spell that then will let me empower Jace. Maybe draw a card if I kill a three toughness thing.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Violent Echoes.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Jiang Yanggu, Never Alone is better than Jiang Yanggu, Alone (four-drop versus five-drop, five-five of stats across two bodies), but the card gets worse in multiples because the bodies stick around.
ideas.quote: This is the sort of card that gets worse in multiples because the bodies tend to stick around.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Jiang Yanggu, Never Alone by copy count.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Prefer the red-green land to an extra removal spell when early creatures are low-power: Rockfall Vale over Compel Brutality, because bad mana is one of the ways you lose and he already has three or four burn spells.
ideas.quote: one of the ways you lose is by having bad mana. And I feel like this card is going to do a lot of work for me.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Rockfall Vale in red-green decks against Compel Brutality.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A Konstrari Improviser is the ramp he hoped to see: it gets him to Kiora and the Yanggus and works with his artifact tokens.
ideas.quote: I love the Constrai improviser. I was hoping to see some of these. Just get myself some ramp.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Konstrari Improviser in ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: The question for a good card at pick 8 is not whether it is good but whether it beats the card you end up cutting, and whether it beats a basic land: he takes a land over Bestial Incursion.
ideas.quote: the question is, is bestial incursion going to be better than the card I end up cutting
ideas.test_idea: Rate at which a pick-8 playable makes the 23 when the deck already has 20 playables.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Jiang Yanggu works in multiples because you can discard one to the other, so he keeps taking them.
ideas.quote: They work well in multiples because you can discard the one to the other.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks with two Jiang Yanggu, Alone.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Take a card you want to try over a better-fitting one when the deck is already strong: Emrakul, the Exigent Doom first pick of pack 3 over Konstrari Improviser.
ideas.quote: I could take Constrampt Improviser. It might just be better for my deck, but I'm going to take this thing because I really want to try it out.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Emrakul, the Exigent Doom.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Early acceleration over a fourth removal spell when removal is already sufficient (Wrath, Forte, Echoes, No Admittance, Sureshot): Heartwood Crafter again.
ideas.quote: my removal suite is looking pretty reasonable right now. I would rather just get like early acceleration to get to my top end cards a little faster.
ideas.test_idea: Marginal value of the fifth removal spell against a ramp creature.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A third copy of Heartwood Crafter gets worse: he does not want to flood on that effect, and Compel Brutality fills out his removal suite as the fifth removal spell.
ideas.quote: I think heartwood cracfter the third copy does get a little bit worse. You don't want to get too flooded on this sort of effect.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks by Heartwood Crafter copy count.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: In best of three Flourishing Grapple would be a great sideboard card, but in best of one he takes a deck card.
ideas.quote: If this was best of three, I would take flourishing grapple as a great sideboard card.
ideas.test_idea: Not testable on best-of-one data; record only.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Samut, Hazoret's Champion over No Admittance: even if a mistake, it makes his whole deck better (Yanggu can attack immediately), and it has done a lot of work against him.
ideas.quote: I'm going to take this over no admittance. It might be a mistake honestly, but I feel like it's just done so much work in games against me.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Samut, Hazoret's Champion against No Admittance in red-green.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Cut Tam's Resistance first: the deck has enough two-drops and early things to do; Budding Insurgent, Hallway Heckler, Tether Technician and Wrecking Gecko are cut as he prefers Jiang Yanggu to get rid of extra lands; with 17 creatures he is comfortable.
ideas.quote: I'd rather have Jiang Yangu to be my getting rid of extra lands card.
ideas.test_idea: Creature count (16 / 17 / 18) against win rate in ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Not splashing: with a pure red-green value deck he keeps Emrakul as the poster child and biases towards green because the double-green Fblthp makes it easy to get the next colour.
ideas.quote: It's just a pure red green kind of value deck.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of two-colour against splash decks in red-green.
